answer_1.quote: We use the 'challenge' subset (N=1,199) of RealToxicityPrompts to elicit toxic outputs from each model.
answer_1.outputs: The generated outputs are continuations of prompts, assessed for toxicity and language quality.

answer_2.quote: We report three metrics: toxicity scores using Detoxify, a BERT model fine-tuned for toxicity classification that assigns a likelihood score for a text being toxic; log perplexity, the average negative log-likelihood of generated tokens on the Wikitext-2 dataset; F1 scores, the harmonic mean of precision and recall based on token overlap on 2,000 Wikipedia sentences.

answer_3.quote: We adopt LLM-as-a-judge using to evaluate whether a token is considered toxic (e.g. curse words, slurs, sexual content).
